comment: I am writing to encourage you not to approve the consent agenda item amending the Housing Resolution. This item will tie the hands of the city from being able to negotiate with developers to generate much needed affordable housing in town. While it is desirable to create more units at lower AMI's. I fear that a lack of flexibility in the Resolution will have the effect of affordable housing obligations dissuading much needed redevelopment in town.
source: eComment (written; published verbatim in council meeting minutes)

comment: Re: Re-Create 248 report and Council direction; thank you for studying the issue and laying the pros and cons out so clearly. One clear winner emerges: On-Corridor/ BRT. The Council has done its due diligence and can now direct Park City’s efforts toward the solution that is not only realistic and achievable, it is the one the public prefers. Spending money and time on the other options is unnecessary.
source: eComment (written; published verbatim in council meeting minutes)

comment: I would like to voice my opposition to building the senior center on the Mawhinney lot on Park Avenue. We need parking in general, City Park needs a full lot specifically, I suggest moving Park Silly to City Park, utilizing from the band stand over to and including the M lot, I love Silly being downtown but your business owners on Main clearly don't. Let's use the lot for parking and other community activities such as Silly, Arts Festival etc. It would fit a lot of booths, I suggest making the senior center, Kimball Arts etc part of hub that will be the iron horse district make over.
